payments.title: Payments
payments.subtitle: What you are owed and what has been paid
payments.summary: Record the payments you receive and know, at any moment, how much each customer owes you.
payments.pointRecord: Record a payment against one or several delivery notes, in cash, transfer or foreign currency.
payments.pointBalance: Outstanding balance per customer, derived from documents and payments, never typed in.
payments.pointCreditLimit: Switch on the credit limit, which is already implemented and never fires today.
payments.pointAging: Debt ageing: what has been outstanding for more than 30, 60 and 90 days.
payments.why: It is the next module, and the one whose absence shows most. The credit limit is already written and tested in the business rules, but the outstanding-balance query always returns zero because there are no payments to subtract: the rule exists and never fires. It was left out to get a complete buy-sell-report cycle first.
payments.meanwhile: Each customer credit limit can already be recorded on their record, ready for when the module lands:

quotes.title: Quotes
quotes.subtitle: What you offer before dispatching
quotes.summary: Send a customer a quote and turn it into a delivery note when they accept, without typing it again.
quotes.pointDraft: Same lines and same totals as a delivery note, with its exchange rate frozen.
quotes.pointNoStock: It moves no stock: a quote dispatches nothing, it only commits a price.
quotes.pointConvert: An expiry date, and one-click conversion into a delivery note when the customer says yes.
quotes.why: The numbering already covers them and the document looks a lot like a delivery note. Two things differ — it moves no stock and it expires — and those are exactly what prevents reusing the rules as they are. Finishing the document that does move goods came first.
quotes.meanwhile: To put a price in writing you can issue the delivery note once the sale closes:

purchaseOrders.title: Purchase orders
purchaseOrders.subtitle: What you ordered before it arrives
purchaseOrders.summary: Put in writing what you asked a supplier for, and see what is still to arrive.
purchaseOrders.pointOrder: The order with its lines and agreed cost, before anything enters stock.
purchaseOrders.pointPartial: Partial receipts against the same order: ten of twenty arrive and get recorded.
purchaseOrders.pointPending: What is ordered and has not arrived, which is half the question when restocking.
purchaseOrders.why: It is a declared cut, not an oversight. For a small shop what moves the business is recording what arrived; ordering formally beforehand is a flow for companies with a purchasing department. The buy, stock and sell cycle is closed without it.
purchaseOrders.meanwhile: Record the goods receipt when it arrives, which is what updates stock:

waking.title: Waking the server
waking.lead: The data service was asleep. Free hosting shuts it down after fifteen minutes without visitors, and it takes about a minute to come back.
waking.explain: This happens once. From now on the app responds instantly while you are using it.
waking.stuck: This is taking longer than usual. You can wait a bit more or try again.
